newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland, India sign agreements to strengthen ties.
newsitem.headline: Poland, India sign agreements to strengthen ties.

text.p: Poland and India signed agreements to boost economic, security and cultural cooperation on Monday on the first day of Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma's official visit, PAP news agency said.

Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski said after meeting Sharma that Indian former leader Mahatma Gandhi's idea of non-violence had often been an inspiration for Poland, which peacefully overthrew communism in 1989.
"We have on many occasions referred to the ideas of the great Mahatma Gandhi in calls for political changes without violence," PAP quoted Kwasniewski as saying.
The presidents earlier witnessed the signing of agreements on mutual protection of investment, cultural and scientific exchanges and joint efforts to combat organised crime.
Polish presidential spokesman Antoni Styrczula told reporters the Indian president hoped the two countries would soon sign an agreement on bank guarantees.

Polish-Indian trade tumbled after the fall of communism, when the two countries abandoned barter exchanges. It began to grow in 1992 and reached $186 million last year compared to $129 million in 1994.
Sharma, who leads a 130-strong delegation of politicians and business executives, was due to meet Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz and to visit Warsaw monuments.

On Tuesday, the last day of his visit, Sharma is scheduled to visit the former Nazi German death camp of Auschwitz to pay tribute to about 1.5 million people, mostly Jews, murdered there during World War Two.
